capstone.brief: Take control of your money in 30 days. Track every naira or dollar you spend, build a budget you can live with, save a starter emergency fund, and pay down one debt. Report your numbers honestly at the end.
checks: One debt paid down or a payoff plan started
Money goals written for the next 90 days
One money habit kept for the full 30 days
capstone.title: Take Control of Your Money in 30 Days

course.tagline: Take control of your money: budgets, saving and getting out of debt.
course.title: Personal Finance and Budgeting

days.challenge: Write down every single thing you spent money on yesterday.
days.goal: See clearly where your money goes each month.

quiz.explain: Personal finance means how you earn, spend, save and manage your money.
options: How you earn, spend, save and manage your money
quiz.q: What is personal finance?

quiz.explain: Most people do not know where their money goes, because small spends add up quietly.
quiz.q: Why do most people not know where their money goes?

quiz.explain: Seeing your spending clearly is the first step to changing it.
options: Seeing your spending is the first step to changing it
You should never look at spending
quiz.q: Why track your spending first?

steps: Watch the video and write what personal finance means in your own words.
Write down how much money you get each month.
Write down your five biggest monthly costs.
Write down three small things you buy often without thinking.
Add up the small things for one month. You may be surprised.
Write one sentence about what you want to change.
days.task: Write down your monthly income, your five biggest costs, and three small daily spends.
days.title: Know Where Your Money Goes

video.title: Budgeting for Beginners: Why Most People Fail (And How to Fix It)

days.challenge: Track every spend today, even the smallest one.
days.goal: Track every spend for one full day.

quiz.explain: Tracking means writing down every spend, with the amount and what it was for.
options: Writing down every spend with amount and reason
Checking your bank once a month
quiz.q: What does tracking your spending mean?

quiz.explain: Small spends add up to a lot over a month, so they matter.
options: Small spends add up to a lot over a month
quiz.q: Why track small spends too?

quiz.explain: A notes app on your phone is the easiest tracker, because it is always with you.
options: A notes app on your phone is always with you
A paper book you leave at home
A bank statement once a year
quiz.q: What is the easiest way to track spending?

steps: Open a notes app on your phone and make a list called Spending.
Every time you spend money today, write the amount and what it was for.
Include small things: snacks, transport, airtime.
At night, add up the total for the day.
Circle the spends you could have skipped.
Write one sentence about what surprised you.
days.task: Track every spend today in your phone, add it up, and circle what you could skip.
days.title: Track Spending for One Day

video.title: Budgeting for Beginners - How to Make a Budget From Scratch Today

days.challenge: List ten things you bought last month and mark each one need or want.
days.goal: Tell needs and wants apart, in plain words.

quiz.explain: A need is something you must have to live and work, like food, rent and transport.
options: Something you must have to live and work
quiz.q: What is a need?

quiz.explain: A want is something nice to have, but you can live without it.
options: Something nice to have, but you can live without it
quiz.q: What is a want?

quiz.explain: Wants are not bad, but they should come after needs and savings are covered.
options: Wants should come after needs and savings
quiz.q: Where do wants fit in your budget?

steps: List ten things you bought last month.
Mark each one N for need or W for want.
Add up the money spent on wants.
Ask yourself: which wants were worth it, and which were not?
Pick one want to cut or reduce next month.
Write down how much money that will save you.
days.task: Mark last month's buys as needs or wants, add up the wants, and pick one to cut.
days.title: Needs vs Wants

video.title: Personal Financial Planning Explained | Complete Budgeting, Savings, Financial Goals

days.challenge: Write your goal on a card and put it in your wallet.
days.goal: Set one clear money goal you can measure.

quiz.explain: A good money goal is clear, has a number, and has a date.
options: A clear goal with a number and a date
quiz.q: What makes a good money goal?

quiz.explain: Save 50,000 naira in three months has a number and a date, so you can check it.
quiz.q: Which of these is a clear money goal?

quiz.explain: A goal with a date gives you a reason to act now, not someday.
options: A date gives you a reason to act now
quiz.q: Why give your goal a date?

steps: Think of one thing you want money for: an emergency fund, a debt, or a big buy.
Write the goal with a number: for example, save 50,000 naira.
Write the date you want it done by.
Work out how much to save each week to reach it.
Write the goal on a card and keep it where you will see it.
Tell one person about your goal so they can cheer you on.
days.task: Write one money goal with a number and a date, and work out the weekly saving needed.
days.title: Set One Money Goal

video.title: How to Budget for Beginners (Your Brain Isn't Built for Money)

days.challenge: Split last month's spending into 50, 30 and 20 and see how close you are.
days.goal: Understand the 50/30/20 rule for splitting your money.

quiz.explain: The 50/30/20 rule splits your money: 50 percent for needs, 30 percent for wants, 20 percent for saving and debt.
options: 50 percent for fun, 30 for bills, 20 for shopping
50 for needs, 30 for wants, 20 for saving and debt
50 for saving, 30 for wants, 20 for needs
50 for debt, 30 for needs, 20 for fun
quiz.q: What is the 50/30/20 rule?

quiz.explain: It is a simple starting guide, not a strict law. Adjust it to fit your real life.
options: It is a simple starting guide you can adjust
It works only for rich people
quiz.q: Is the 50/30/20 rule a strict law?

quiz.explain: Saving 20 percent builds safety and freedom over time.
options: Saving 20 percent builds safety and freedom
Saving is only for old people
quiz.q: Why save 20 percent?

steps: Write down your monthly income.
Work out 50 percent, 30 percent and 20 percent of it.
Put your needs under 50 percent: rent, food, transport, bills.
Put your wants under 30 percent: fun, eating out, clothes.
Put saving and extra debt payments under 20 percent.
Compare with your real spending from day 1. Where are you over?
days.task: Split your income into 50/30/20 and compare it with your real spending.
days.title: The 50/30/20 Rule

video.title: Personal Finance for Beginners: Budgeting, Money Management & Financial Literacy | Full Audiobook

days.challenge: Write your budget in 15 minutes using only your phone notes.
days.goal: Make your first monthly budget.

quiz.explain: A budget is a simple plan that says where your money will go before you spend it.
options: A plan that says where your money will go before you spend it
quiz.q: What is a budget?

quiz.explain: A budget gives every naira or dollar a job, so money does not just disappear.
options: A budget is only for poor people
A budget gives every unit of money a job
quiz.q: Why make a budget?

quiz.explain: A budget that is too strict fails fast. A realistic one you can keep is better.
options: A realistic budget you can keep is better than a strict one
quiz.q: Why keep your budget realistic?

steps: Write your monthly income at the top.
List your needs with amounts: rent, food, transport, bills.
List your wants with a limit for each one.
Write your saving amount: aim for 20 percent, or start smaller.
Add everything up. It must not be more than your income.
If it is more, cut wants first until it fits.
days.task: Write your first monthly budget with income, needs, wants and saving.
days.title: Make Your First Budget

video.title: How to Actually Change Your Finances in 6 Months

days.challenge: Show your budget to a friend and ask if it looks realistic.
days.goal: Put your income, spending, goal and budget together on one page.

project.brief: Build your first monthly budget on one page: your income, your needs, your wants, your saving, and your money goal. Check that the numbers add up and the budget is one you can actually live with.
checks: One friend or family member has seen it
project.title: Your First Monthly Budget

quiz.explain: A good budget covers needs, limits wants, includes saving, and fits your income.
options: A budget that covers needs, limits wants, includes saving, fits income
A budget that spends more than income
quiz.q: What does a good first budget look like?

quiz.explain: Showing your budget to someone you trust adds honesty and support.
options: Showing it adds honesty and support
quiz.q: Why show your budget to someone you trust?

quiz.explain: A budget is a plan you adjust as life changes, not a one-time test.
options: A budget is a plan you adjust as life changes
quiz.q: What do you do when your budget does not work perfectly?

steps: Put your income at the top of the page.
Add your needs, wants and saving from day 6.
Add your money goal from day 4.
Check the total fits your income.
Read it out loud and ask: can I live with this for one month?
Show it to someone you trust and fix anything unrealistic.
days.task: Finish your one-page monthly budget with income, needs, wants, saving and goal.
days.title: Week 1 Project: Your First Monthly Budget

video.title: Personal Finance for Beginners: 7 Rules to Fix Your Money

days.challenge: Cut one daily spend for a week and see how much you save.
days.goal: Cut spending without feeling miserable.

quiz.explain: Cut the big, painless things first: subscriptions you do not use, eating out often, and impulse buys.
options: Cut unused subscriptions, frequent eating out, impulse buys
quiz.q: What is the easiest spending to cut first?

quiz.explain: Small daily spends add up to a lot, so cutting one can save real money.
options: Small daily spends add up to a lot
quiz.q: Why cut small daily spends?
What is an impulse buy?
options: A buy you make without thinking, on the spot
quiz.explain: An impulse buy is something you buy on the spot without planning, and it adds up fast.

steps: List three things you buy often that you could reduce.
Pick one to cut completely for a week.
Pick one to cut in half for a week.
Write down how much each cut saves you in a week.
Put the saved money straight into your savings.
At the end of the week, decide if the cut was easy or hard.
days.task: Cut one spend for a week and one spend in half, and save the money.
days.title: Cut Spending Without Suffering

video.title: 50/30/20 Rule Explained: Budgeting for Beginners

days.challenge: Save 1,000 naira or 5 dollars today, right now.
days.goal: Save money first, before you spend it.

quiz.explain: Pay yourself first means moving money to savings the day you get paid, before spending.
options: Spending first, saving what is left
Moving money to savings the day you get paid, before spending
quiz.q: What does pay yourself first mean?

quiz.explain: Money left at month end usually gets spent, so saving first is the only way it happens.
options: Money left over always gets saved
Money left over usually gets spent
It does not matter when you save
quiz.q: Why save first instead of saving what is left?

quiz.explain: Even a small amount saved often grows into a useful sum over time.
options: Even small regular savings grow into something useful
quiz.q: Why does saving a small amount still matter?

steps: Decide your saving amount for this month.
Set the day you get paid as your saving day.
Move the money to savings on that day, before you spend anything.
If you cannot move it by hand, set an automatic transfer.
Write down the date and amount in your notes.
Tell yourself: this money is for my future, not for today.
days.task: Move your saving amount to savings today, before you spend anything else.
days.title: Save First, Spend Later

video.title: Smart Budgeting in Excel - Save More and Balance Income and Expenses

days.challenge: Save your first emergency 5,000 naira or 25 dollars this week.
days.goal: Start a small emergency fund for surprise costs.

quiz.explain: An emergency fund is money set aside for surprise costs like a broken phone or a hospital visit.
options: Money set aside for surprise costs
quiz.q: What is an emergency fund?

quiz.explain: Start with one small goal, like one month of basic costs, then grow it.
options: Save a full year at once
Start small, like one month of basic costs, then grow it
quiz.q: How big should your first emergency fund be?

quiz.explain: An emergency fund stops a surprise bill from becoming a debt.
options: An emergency fund stops a surprise bill becoming a debt
quiz.q: Why does an emergency fund matter?

steps: Work out your basic monthly costs: food, transport and bills.
Set your first emergency goal: one month of those costs.
Open a separate savings account or a locked savings spot.
Put your first amount in today, even if it is small.
Write the goal and the date you want to reach it.
Add to it every payday, even a little.
days.task: Open a separate emergency savings spot and put your first amount in.
days.title: Build a Small Emergency Fund

video.title: Why Budgets Don't Work - and How You Can Change That

days.challenge: Set up an automatic transfer for your next payday.
days.goal: Automate your savings so you never forget.

quiz.explain: Automating savings means your bank moves the money for you on payday, without you thinking about it.
options: Your bank moves the money for you on payday
Asking a friend to save for you
quiz.q: What does automating your savings mean?

quiz.explain: Automatic saving happens every time, even when you are busy or tempted to spend.
options: It happens every time, even when you are busy
It is hard to set up
It only works for rich people
quiz.q: Why automate your savings?

quiz.explain: Start with a small amount you can keep, then raise it when your income grows.
options: Start small and raise it later
You should never change the amount
quiz.q: How much should you automate at first?

steps: Open your bank app and find the automatic transfer option.
Set a transfer from your main account to your savings.
Set the date to your payday.
Set the amount to your saving amount from day 9.
Check it is set correctly.
Write down the date and amount in your notes.
days.task: Set up an automatic transfer to savings for your next payday.
days.title: Automate Your Savings

video.title: Budgeting for Beginners: Why Most People Fail (And How to Fix It)

days.challenge: Find three money leaks in your spending from last week.
days.goal: Find and plug small money leaks.

quiz.explain: A money leak is a small, repeated spend you barely notice, like daily snacks or unused subscriptions.
options: A small repeated spend you barely notice
A bank fee you cannot avoid
quiz.q: What is a money leak?

quiz.explain: Leaks add up quietly over a month, so finding them saves real money.
options: Leaks add up quietly over a month
Leaks are only for rich people
quiz.q: Why do money leaks matter?

quiz.explain: Cancel or cut the leak, then move the saved money to your savings.
options: Cancel or cut it, then save the money
quiz.q: What do you do when you find a leak?

steps: Open your spending notes from the last week.
Circle every spend under a small amount that repeats daily.
List the top three leaks.
Cancel or cut each one: unsubscribe, cook instead of buying, walk instead of riding.
Work out how much you save in a month.
Move that money to your savings.
days.task: Find three money leaks, cut them, and move the savings to your emergency fund.
days.title: Kill Small Money Leaks

video.title: Budgeting for Beginners - How to Make a Budget From Scratch Today

days.challenge: Use cash for one week for all small buys and see what changes.
days.goal: Try the cash envelope method for one spending area.

quiz.explain: The envelope method means putting cash for one spending area in an envelope, and stopping when it is empty.
options: Putting cash for one area in an envelope, stopping when empty
quiz.q: What is the cash envelope method?

quiz.explain: Cash feels real, so you notice spending it more than tapping a card.
options: Cash feels real, so you notice spending it
quiz.q: Why does using cash help some people spend less?

quiz.explain: Try it for one area, like food or fun, not for everything at once.
options: Try it for one area first
Use cash for everything at once
Cash is only for old people
quiz.q: How should you start with envelopes?

steps: Pick one spending area: food, fun or transport.
Work out your weekly amount for it from your budget.
Take that amount in cash and put it in an envelope.
Spend only from that envelope for one week.
When it is empty, stop spending in that area.
Write down how it felt compared to using a card.
days.task: Use a cash envelope for one spending area for one week.
days.title: Cash Envelopes: A Simple Trick

video.title: Personal Financial Planning Explained | Complete Budgeting, Savings, Financial Goals

days.challenge: Save your first 10,000 naira or 50 dollars and tell someone about it.
days.goal: Reach your first savings milestone.

project.brief: Reach your first savings milestone: save 10,000 naira or 50 dollars in your emergency fund by the end of this week, using the cuts and leaks you found. Record where the money came from.
checks: Money came from real cuts, not new debt
One cut that worked best noted
project.title: Save Your First 10,000

quiz.explain: A milestone is a small, clear savings target that proves you can do it.
options: A small, clear savings target that proves you can do it
quiz.q: What is a savings milestone?

quiz.explain: Small wins build confidence and the habit of saving.
options: Small wins build confidence and the saving habit
quiz.q: Why celebrate a small savings win?

quiz.explain: Set the next goal right away so the habit keeps going.
options: Set the next goal right away
Wait a year for the next goal
quiz.q: What do you do after reaching a milestone?

steps: Check your emergency fund balance today.
Work out how much more you need to reach 10,000 naira or 50 dollars.
Use your cuts and leaks from days 8 and 12 to find the money.
Put the money in your emergency fund.
Write down where each part came from.
Set your next milestone and its date.
days.task: Reach your first savings milestone and record where the money came from.
days.title: Week 2 Project: Save Your First 10,000

days.challenge: List every debt you have, even the small ones you forgot.
days.goal: Understand debt: what it is and what it costs you.

quiz.explain: Debt is money you borrowed that you must pay back, usually with extra money called interest.
options: Money you borrowed that you must pay back, usually with interest
quiz.q: What is debt?

quiz.explain: Interest is the extra money you pay for borrowing, on top of what you borrowed.
options: The extra money you pay for borrowing
quiz.q: What is interest?

quiz.explain: High interest debt grows fast, so it should be paid first.
options: High interest debt grows fast, so pay it first
quiz.q: Why pay high interest debt first?

steps: List every debt you have: loans, borrowed money, buy-now-pay-later.
For each one, write the amount you owe and the interest rate.
Add up the total you owe.
Work out how much interest you pay each month.
Circle the debt with the highest interest rate.
Write down how it feels to see the full list.
days.task: List all your debts with amounts and interest rates, and add up the total.

video.title: Personal Finance for Beginners: Budgeting, Money Management & Financial Literacy | Full Audiobook

days.challenge: Pay a little extra on your smallest debt today, even a tiny amount.
days.goal: Make a simple debt payoff plan.

quiz.explain: The snowball method pays the smallest debt first for quick wins, then moves to the next.
options: Pay the smallest debt first for quick wins
quiz.q: What is the debt snowball method?

quiz.explain: The avalanche method pays the highest interest debt first, which saves the most money.
options: Pay the highest interest debt first to save the most money
quiz.q: What is the debt avalanche method?

quiz.explain: Both methods work. Pick the one you will actually stick with.
options: Pick the one you will actually stick with
quiz.q: Which debt method should you pick?

steps: Look at your debt list from day 15.
Pick your method: smallest first for quick wins, or highest interest first to save money.
Write your debts in payoff order.
Work out a monthly payment for the first debt, even a small extra amount.
Pay the minimum on all debts, and extra on the first one.
Write the date you expect the first debt to be gone.
days.task: Write your debt payoff order and pay extra on the first debt this month.

days.challenge: Go one week without borrowing for a want.
days.goal: Stop using debt for wants.

quiz.explain: Borrowing for wants means paying interest on things you could live without, which keeps you poor.
options: It keeps you poor because you pay interest on non-essentials
quiz.q: Why is borrowing for wants a bad idea?

quiz.explain: Save for wants instead, so you pay no interest and feel no stress.
options: Save for wants instead, so you pay no interest
quiz.q: What should you do instead of borrowing for wants?

quiz.explain: Waiting 30 days before a big want shows if you really want it or just felt a rush.
options: Waiting 30 days shows if you really want it
quiz.q: Why wait 30 days before a big want?

steps: Write down three wants you bought with borrowed money before.

Write your new rule: no borrowing for wants, only for real needs.
Make a wants list: write a want down and wait 30 days before buying.
If you still want it after 30 days, save for it.
Tell one person about your new rule.

days.challenge: Check your credit report or ask your bank about your credit record.
days.goal: Understand credit and how to build it safely.

options: Borrowing with a promise to pay back
quiz.q: What is credit?

options: Borrowing small and paying back on time
quiz.q: How do you build good credit?

quiz.explain: Missing payments hurts your record and makes future borrowing harder and costlier.
options: Missing payments hurts your record and future borrowing
quiz.q: Why do late payments hurt you?

Check your record if you can.
Write down any late payments or problems you see.
Write your rule: always pay at least the minimum on time.
If you have a small loan or card, pay it on time every month.
Write down one step to improve your record this year.

days.challenge: Write your one-year money goals on a card and keep it visible.
days.goal: Set money goals for the next year.

quiz.explain: Good goals have a number, a date, and a clear reason.
options: A number, a date, and a clear reason
quiz.q: What makes a good money goal?

quiz.explain: Short goals are for months, medium goals for a year or two, long goals for many years.
options: Short for months, medium for a year or two, long for many years

options: Breaking a big goal into monthly steps makes it possible
Goals should never be broken down

Put the three goals on one card where you will see them.

quiz.q: Why automate your bills?

Pay extra on the first debt in your order.
